Ps 26 confirmed identity numbering (web_verses=mt_verses=12, mt_title_verses=[]). Both cited Hebrew phrases collate at BYTE tier against oshb:Ps.26.1 and oshb:Ps.26.11, and the repeated phrase 'in my integrity I have/will walk[ed]' is a real, byte-confirmed inclusio-type repetition bracketing the psalm -- a legitimate corroborating observation. However, device_notes misstates where in each verse the phrase actually sits. It claims 'V. 1 opens בְּתֻמִּ֣י הָלַ֑כְתִּי,' but the full verse bytes (לְדָוִ֨ד שָׁפְטֵ֤נִי יְהוָ֗ה כִּֽי אֲ֭נִי בְּתֻמִּ֣י הָלַ֑כְתִּי וּבַיהוָ֥ה בָּ֝טַ֗חְתִּי לֹ֣א אֶמְעָֽד) show the verse actually opens with the plea 'Judge me, Yahweh, for I...', matching WEB's own word order ('Judge me, Yahweh, for I have walked in my integrity') -- the integrity clause is medial (the verse's 6th-7th word), not its opening. Symmetrically it claims 'V. 11 closes בְּתֻמִּ֥י אֵלֵ֗ךְ,' but Ps.26.11 (וַ֭אֲנִי בְּתֻמִּ֥י אֵלֵ֗ךְ פְּדֵ֣נִי וְחָנֵּֽנִי) continues with 'redeem me, and be merciful to me' after the integrity clause, so the phrase is not the verse's close either. This is a factual, checkable misstatement of textual position, not a matter of interpretation. See challenge LF-064-1.
